description: Application under S73 of Town and Country Planning Act 1990 to carry out development without compliance with Condition 9 (Use Class) of Planning Permission 17/16773/FUL (Redevelopment of the site to provide 36 flats (13 x1 bed, 19 x 2 bed and 4 x 3 bed), 2 retail units, 3 live/work units, doctors surgery and basement level car park) to allow the use of the ground floor unit originally designated as doctors surgery (Class D1 to be used as a health centre or health clinic within Use Class D1, associated with use as a doctors or dental surgery, physiotherapy, chiropractic or orthopaedic clinic) to allow uses within Classes E(a), E ( c), E (e) and E(g)(i) of the Town and Country Planning (Use Class Order) 1987 as amended and Town and County Planning (Use Classes) (Amendment) (England) Regulations 2020.
decision_conditions: Petrol/oil interceptors should be fitted to all car parking facilities.Reason: Failure to enforce the effective use of Petrol/Oil interceptors could result in oil-polluted discharges entering the local watercourse, contrary to Policy DM4 (Water management and Flood Risk) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

Development shall be implemented and maintained in accordance with the drainage strategy approved under reference 12/16317COND.Reason: To ensure that the foul and/or surface water discharge from the site shall not be prejudicial to the existing sewerage system in terms of causing localised flooding and pollution of the water environment in accordance with Policy DM4 (Water management and Flood Risk) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

All site works shall be in accordance with the details approved under reference 09/16381COND.Reason: In order to safeguard the amenities of the surrounding residential occupiers and to safeguard highway safety and the free flow of traffic in accordance with Policy DM10 (Design Requirements for New Developments including House Extensions) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

All works shall take place in accordance with the method statement approved under reference 12/16317/COND.Reason: In the interests of the amenities of the area in accordance with Policy DM10 (Design Requirements for New Developments including House Extensions) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

All decontamination works shall take place in accordance with the method statement approved under reference 12/16317/COND.Reason: To prevent pollution of the water environment in accordance with Policy DM4 (Water management and Flood Risk) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

No flues or pipework, shall be fixed to the elevations other than those shown on the drawings hereby approved or in accordance with details which shall have first been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: In the interests of the visual amenities of the area in accordance with Policy DM10 (Design Requirements for New Developments including House Extensions) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

The development shall include the acoustic insulation measures to the ground floor commercial units approved as under application 12/16318/COND and shall thereafter be permanently retained.Reason: In order to control the noise emanating there from and in the interests of the residential amenities of the area in accordance with Policy DM10 (Design Requirements for New Developments including House Extensions) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

Notwithstanding Section 55 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended) and the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended) (or any Order revoking and reenacting that Order with or without modification),The ground floor retail unit(s) Units (other than Unit 3) shall only be used for- Class E (a) - Display or retail sale of goods, Class E ( c) - no other purposes whatsoever (including any other purposes falling within Class E of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987  and  the  Town and  Country Planning (Use Classes) (Amendment) (England) Regulations 2020 (or any provision equivalent to that class in any Order revoking and reenacting that Order with or without modification).Reason: The acceptability of the development is highly dependent upon the exact nature of the use of the site and other uses, whether within the same use class or permitted by the General Permitted Development Order, are unlikely to be acceptable in planning terms within the development shall be used only for the listed usesand for no other use within Class E of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987, or other succeeding legislation, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority. In the interests of strengthening the retail attractions of this part of the district shopping centre and the vitality and viability of the shopping centre as a whole and in the interests of the protecting the amenities of both existingand future neighbouring residents in accordance with Policies CS12 and DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

Notwithstanding Section 55 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended) and the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended) (or any Order revoking and reenacting that Order with or without modification), the premises  (identified as Unit 3, 30 Old Post Office Walk, Surbiton, KT6 4JF) shall only be used for the purposes specified in the application documents and Application Form Class E (a) - Display or retail sale of goods,Class E (c) - Financial and professional services,Class E (e) - medical or health services  and Class E (g) (i) -  (office) and for no other purposes whatsoever (including any other purposes falling within Class E of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987  and  the  Town and  Country Planning (Use Classes) (Amendment) (England) Regulations 2020 (or any provision equivalent to that class in any Order revoking and reenacting that Order with or without modification).Reason: The acceptability of the development is highly dependent upon the exact nature of the use of the site and other uses, whether within the same use class or permitted by the General Permitted Development Order, are unlikely to be acceptable in planning terms.

Any broadcasting or amplifying equipment to be installed on the ground floor of the development shall at no time be audible outside the curtilage of the unit(s).Reason: To safeguard the amenities of the occupiers of the neighbouring properties in accordance with Policy DM10 (Design Requirements for New Developments including House Extensions) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

The ground floor units shall not be used for the purposes hereby permitted before 7.30am or after 11.30pm Monday to Saturday or before 9.00am or after 10.30pm on Sundays.Reason: To safeguard the amenities of the occupiers of the neighbouring properties in accordance with Policy DM10 (Design Requirements for New Developments including House Extensions) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.
A shop window display must be maintained at all times in Units 1 and 2.Reason: In order to maintain the continuity and interest of the shopping frontage in accordance with Policies CS12 and DM10

The roof and emergency access/escape to the rear of Block 6 incorporating the work/live units shall not be converted or used as a balcony or sitting out area and shall be used only for the purposes of emergency escape from the premises and for maintenance purposes.Reason: To protect the amenities and privacy of the adjoining residential properties in accordance with Policy DM10 (Design Requirements for New Developments including House Extensions) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

The work part of the live/work units hereby approved shall be used for no other purpose than uses falling within Class E(g) of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended), or other succeeding legislation, which can be carried out in association with the residential part of the units, shown on the submitted plans hereby approved without detriment to the amenity of neighbouring residents, and shall not be used for any other purpose without the prior written consent of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure that the unit is used for its authorised purpose in order to maintain local employment on this site and without detriment to the amenities of neighbouring residents in accordance with Policies DM17 and DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

The live/work units shall not be occupied for residential purposes unless the unit is also being occupied for business purposes by the same occupier.Reason: In order to ensure that the unit is used for its authorised purpose in order to maintain local employment on this site in accordance with Policy DM17 of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

Each live/work unit shall be occupied as a single integrated unit and shall not be subdivided without the prior written consent of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: In order to ensure that the employment use of the building is safeguarded and not lost through subdivision of the building in accordance with Policy DM17 of the LDF ore Strategy Adopted April 2012.

The work element of the work/live units shall be located at ground floor level only.Reason: To protect neighbouring residential amenities in accordance with Policy DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

All planting, seeding or turfing detailed in the landscape scheme approved under reference 12/16317/COND shall be carried out in the first planting and seeding seasons following the occupation of the buildings or the completion of the development, whichever is the sooner; and any trees or plants which, within a period of 5 years from the completion of the development die, are removed or become seriously damaged or diseased shall be replaced in the next planting season with others of similar size and species, unless the Local Planning Authority gives written consent to any variation. The area shown to be landscaped shall be permanently retained for that purpose only.Reason: To ensure that these works are properly implemented and maintained and in the interest of visual amenity in accordance with Policy DM10 (Design Requirements for New Developments including House Extensions) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

The facing materials to be used in the construction of the building shall be those specified within condition discharge 12/16317COND and permanently retained thereafter.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance on completion of the development in accordance with Policy DM10 (Design Requirements for New Developments including House Extensions) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

The building shall be built and maintained in accordance with the agreed panel of brickwork for each of the buildings, as approved as part of condition discharge 12/16317/COND.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance on completion of the development in accordance with Policy DM10 (Design Requirements for New Developments including House Extensions) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

The materials used in the construction of the building shall be the samples agreed as part of condition discharge 12/16317COND.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance on completion of the development in accordance with Policy DM10 (Design Requirements for New Developments including House Extensions) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

Notwithstanding the provisions of Schedule 2 of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 2015, (or any Order revoking or reenacting this Order) no telecommunications equipment shall be erected on the roofs of any of the buildings hereby approved without the prior written consent of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance on completion of the development in accordance with Policies DM10 and DM12 of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

The buildings shall be built and maintained in accordance with the agreed detailed elevations, as approved as part of condition discharge 12/16317/COND.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance on completion of the development in accordance with Policy DM10 (Design Requirements for New Developments including House Extensions) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

The buildings shall be built and maintained in accordance with the agreed specifications relating to:(a) street furniture and lighting(b) sewer and drainage runs(c) any external plant and equipment, including flues and pipework(d) boundary treatment, including details of the boundary wall along the northern boundary of the site with 35-46 Cottage Grove, including its retention and rebuilding/making good works together with samples of materials (including their colour and texture) to be used(e) treatment and layout of all parts of the site not covered by the approved buildings, including hard and soft landscapingall as approved as part of condition discharge 12/16317/COND.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance on completion of the development in accordance with Policy DM10 (Design Requirements for New Developments including House Extensions) of the LDF Core StrategyAdopted April 2012.

The refuse and recycling facilities shall be operated and maintained in accordance with the scheme approved as part of condition discharge 12/16317/COND.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance on completion of the development in accordance with Policy DM10 (Design Requirements for New Developments including House Extensions) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

The servicing arrangements for the Mews shall take place only in accordance with the agreed strategy.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance on completion of the development in accordance with Policy DM10 (Design Requirements for New Developments including House Extensions) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

The widened carriageway and footway shall be retained permanently available for vehicular and pedestrian circulation only.Reason: In order to ensure the safety of occupiers and users of the development in accordance with Policy DM10 (Design Requirements for New Developments including House Extensions) of the LDF Core StrategyAdopted April 2012.

The car park shall be permanently marked out in accordance with the details shown on approved plan PL 13_201 Rev C and shall thereafter be kept free from obstruction and used for car parking purposes only.Reason: In the interests of amenity, the free flow of traffic on the highway and road safety in accordance with Policies DM9 (Managing Vehicle Use for New Development) and Policy DM10 (Design Requirements for New Developments including House Extensions) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

The development shall be implemented and maintained in accordance withan agreed Travel Plan.Reason: To ensure that sustainable transport methods are encouraged and implemented in accordance with Policies CS5 (Reducing the Need to Travel) and CS6 (Sustainable Travel) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

The cycle parking facilities approved as part of condition discharge 12/16317COND shall be fully implemented and thereafter retained for use at all times.Reason: To ensure the provision of satisfactory cycle storage facilities and in the interests of highway safety in accordance with Policy DM8 (Sustainable Transport for New Developments) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.

The sustainability measures and renewable energy measures shall be provided and maintained in accordance with the details approved as part of condition discharge 12/16317COND.Reason: In the interests of sustainability and energy conservation in accordance with Policies 5.2 (Minimising Carbon Dioxide Emissions) and 5.3 (Sustainable Design & Construction) of the London Plan (July 2011) and Policy DM1 (Sustainable Design and Construction Standards) of the LDF Core Strategy Adopted April 2012.
